initial.name: agent_teams_add_member
initial.description: Add a member to the team roster. Planning and idle roster rows do not call a model. After approval, the member session starts with its first ready task or explicit message and remains durable for later work.

name.description: Unique member name inside the team.

role.description: Role of the member (e.g. researcher, engineer, reviewer).

provider.description: Optional LLM provider route. Use only when the user explicitly requests a different provider; requires model. Omit to use the configured member route (memberLlmProvider/memberModel) or the captain's current route.

model.description: Optional model override (used verbatim, including any "/" in the id). Omit for the configured memberModel default (paired with memberLlmProvider when set) or the captain's current model.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort override: one of the target model's supported effort ids, or "default" to force its default. When omitted, the captain's effort is inherited only for the same provider/model; a changed route uses the target default.

executionPrompt.description: Optional member-specific execution prompt. It remains editable while staged.

tool_policy.description: Optional id of a tool policy declared by the deployment owner (config toolPolicies). It restricts which global tools this member sees and may invoke: a policy allow-list also keeps the four coordination tools, and captain-only tools can never be reopened. Omit for the unchanged default tool set.

initial.name: agent_teams_amend_task
initial.description: Captain-only controlled contract amendment for one non-terminal quality task: replace a wrong objective/acceptance/verify/inScope/outOfScope when the original contract makes honest completion impossible (for example a verify command that cannot pass, or an inScope that forbids the file the objective names). The amendment is appended to the task's revisions ledger with previous values and the reason, and is rejected once a review/requirements task has passed judgment on this task. Members cannot amend contracts; the implementer re-reads the amended contract before its next quality gate. Lists are full replacements, not deltas.

task_id.description: Task whose contract is being amended.

reason.description: Why the current contract is wrong; recorded in the revisions ledger.

acceptance.description: Replacement acceptance criteria (full list, not a delta).

verify.description: Replacement verification commands (full list, not a delta).

initial.name: agent_teams_approve
initial.description: Approve and start a staged team plan. Call this only in response to an explicit user approval in a new user turn; never call it during the turn that created or edited the plan. The Web Approve & Run button uses the same runtime directly.

initial.name: agent_teams_claim_task
initial.description: Members claim their own ready task or read their existing attempt_id. Captains must use reassign_task to assign and wake a member; claim_task does not dispatch work. A member cannot own a second unfinished task. The returned attempt_id is required for updates and becomes stale after retry/reassignment.

assignee.description: Deprecated: claim_task only supports a member claiming its own task. Captains must use reassign_task.

initial.name: agent_teams_create
initial.description: Create a team. Use approval=required for a two-phase plan: members and tasks remain unspawned/unclaimed until the user reviews the Web plan and explicitly approves it. Optional profiles expand their configured roster; seed profiles also expand template tasks, while captain profiles leave the graph for the Captain to design. approval=automatic preserves the legacy immediate-execution path.

name.description: Name for the new team (used as its stable id).

description.description: Team purpose / the goal the team will work on.

plan.description: Optional complete ordinary-work roster and DAG in one atomic call, instead of separate add_member/create_task rounds. Mutually exclusive with profile. For quality gates use create_task with the explicit quality contract.

tool_policy.description: Optional owner-declared tool-policy id for this member.

id.description: Local reference used by dependencies in this plan; the result maps it to a durable task id.

approval.description: required stages the plan for explicit user review; automatic starts immediately. Defaults to automatic for API compatibility.

initial.name: agent_teams_create_task
initial.description: Create a task in your team's task list. Use kind=work (default) for research, repository audits and general tasks. kind=review is only a quality gate for an existing implementation/repair task via reviewedTaskId. Every call must include a non-empty subject, including verification and review tasks. Tasks can depend on other tasks (dependencies): a task is only claimable once every dependency is completed. Optionally assign it to a member, who still claims it before working.

subject.description: Required non-empty title for this task. Never omit it, including for verification or review tasks.

description.description: What needs to be done, in detail.

dependencies.description: Task ids this task depends on (must be completed before this task can be claimed).

assignee.description: Member name when an owner is specified. Omission puts this task in the shared pool; roles, subjects and descriptions do not assign an owner.

kind.description: Explicit task kind. Omission means work with no quality gates, even if the subject says implementation/review. Quality kinds require a contract. An implementation may be planned before requirements passes when its dependency chain includes that requirements task.

objective.description: Required non-empty objective for quality kinds.

inScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task may change.

outOfScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task must not change.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria. Required for quality kinds.

reviewedTaskId.description: Existing AgentTeams implementation/repair task id. Required for kind=review; an external repository audit is kind=work.

sourceFindingIds.description: Finding ids this repair must close.

coverageOf.description: User-constraint / goal items this task covers.

resume.description: If true, clear halted in the same lock before creating the task.

initial.name: agent_teams_delete
initial.description: End and archive your team: interrupts members and moves the current tasks and mailboxes out of active state for later inspection. Use when the work is done or explicitly abandoned. A same-name archive replaces its previous generation.

initial.name: agent_teams_edit_plan
initial.description: Atomically revise an AgentTeams plan. While staged, edit tasks and roster without starting work. While running, only update_task is allowed, and only for pending tasks with no prior attempt: correct dependencies, assignees or descriptions before they start; newly ready work is scheduled after commit. Never edit active/finished attempts. Submit dependent edits in order. Never modify .agent-teams files directly.

operations.description: One atomic, ordered batch. Running teams allow only update_task for never-started pending tasks. If any operation is invalid, none of the edits are saved.

member_name.description: Member name for update_member or remove_member.

task_id.description: Task id for update_task or remove_task.

subject.description: Required for add_task; optional replacement for update_task.

assignee.description: Optional task assignee; an empty string moves it to the shared pool.

dependencies.description: Complete replacement dependency list for a task.

provider.description: Optional member provider; defaults to the current staged route.

model.description: Optional member model; defaults to the current staged route.

tool_policy.description: Optional owner-declared tool-policy id for this member; an empty string clears it back to the unchanged default tool set.

initial.name: agent_teams_reassign_task
initial.description: Atomically retry, reassign, or let the captain take over one ready unfinished/failed task. The old attempt is revoked before its member is interrupted, so late updates cannot overwrite the new owner. Use assignee="captain" only when you will finish that task in this turn; a captain can own only one unfinished takeover at a time, and an unfinished takeover returns to the member pool when the captain becomes idle.

assignee.description: Active member name, or "captain" for captain takeover.

reason.description: Why the task is being retried or reassigned.

initial.name: agent_teams_remove_member
initial.description: Remove a member safely: revoke its current attempts, return all unfinished owned tasks to the shared pending pool, interrupt its live turn, and mark it removed.

name.description: Name of the member to remove.

initial.name: agent_teams_resume
initial.description: Explicitly resume a halted team. Requires a non-empty reason. Does not recreate cancelled tasks; only still-pending work is scheduled.

reason.description: Why the team is being resumed.

initial.name: agent_teams_send_message
initial.description: Send coordination or current-task guidance directly to the captain or a teammate. A running recipient receives it at the next model step; an idle recipient wakes. Messages are durably retained until read. Use task creation/reassignment for a new unit of work, not repeated status nudges.

source_task_id.description: Sender task, NOT the recipient task. Members include it with source_attempt_id. Captains sending guidance normally omit both source fields.

source_attempt_id.description: Sender execution capability paired with source_task_id. Stale reports are rejected. Omit for ordinary captain guidance.

from.description: Sender (defaults to the caller: the captain, or the calling member).

initial.name: agent_teams_status
initial.description: Team snapshot: members with live activity and tasks with status/assignee/dependencies/output. Captains also see every team mailbox; members see only their own inbox. Use after mailbox progress deliveries or for an explicit status request. After dispatch, end your turn while members work; do not repeatedly poll.

initial.name: agent_teams_update_task
initial.description: Update a task status/output. Members must supply the current attempt_id returned by claim_task; stale attempts are rejected after takeover/reassignment. Terminal results are immutable, but owners and the captain can append acceptanceResults/commandsRun/evidence_note as attributed supplemental evidence, without reclaiming or changing the verdict. A captain must use reassign_task(assignee="captain") before updating active member-owned work.

attempt_id.description: Members must explicitly include the current attempt_id from their assignment/claim in EVERY update, including failed reviews with findings. If omitted, retry with the same current id; omission does not revoke the attempt.

output.description: Original result summary; immutable after completion/failure.

evidence_note.description: Append-only supplementary observation on a terminal task. Does not reopen work or change the original result.

verdict.description: Required for completing requirements/review. needs_revision and reject must fail the task.

findings.description: Structured review findings. Required when verdict is needs_revision or reject; each item needs id, severity, problem, and requiredFix.

changedPaths.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths changed by this implementation/repair.

acceptanceResults.description: Acceptance evidence in contract order: {criterion, status:"passed"|"failed", evidence?}. Supply one item per acceptance criterion.

commandsRun.description: Verification evidence in contract order: {command, status:"passed"|"failed", exitCode?, evidence?}. Supply one item per verify command.

initial.name: apply_patch
initial.description: Create, update, delete, or move UTF-8 text files with one Codex-style patch; prefer it over multiple edit calls when a change spans several files or separated regions.

input.description: Codex patch text: start with *** Begin Patch and end with *** End Patch. Use *** Add File: path with + lines; *** Update File: path, optionally followed by *** Move to: path, with @@ or @@ context and space-prefixed context, + added, or - removed lines; *** End of File anchors the last hunk to the file end. Use *** Delete File: path to delete. Paths are relative to the Session working directory.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: bash
initial.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: expert_team_list
initial.description: List reusable expert teams and saved experts. Supply query to search bundled experts by role or skill and obtain real catalogue keys. Never invent an expert key or Agent preset.

initial.name: expert_team_save
initial.description: Stage a reusable expert team for a persistent confirmation card. The user reviews and confirms the card before saving. This tool does not save or start agents. Repeated proposals update the same pending card. Select real expertKey values from expert_team_list, or retain a registered agentPreset. Set replace only for an explicitly requested update.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local subagent's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List your entire subagent tree: the root agent and all reachable continuable descendants, including yourself. Rows carry ids, descriptions, and status; descendant rows carry parent ids and depth from the root. You can message any other agent in the subagent tree listed as running or inactive. running means it is working; inactive means no turn is executing; it does not indicate task completion, success, or failure. While you remain active, you will be notified when a direct child finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

initial.name: read
initial.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

initial.name: read_image
initial.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation.

agent_id.description: The agent id of another member of your subagent tree, as shown by list_agents.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. If you are still online when it finishes, the runtime automatically delivers its completion notice. The notice includes the final answer unless the child sent you a message just before finishing. Use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display. Use the language of the user's current request.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

initial.name: subagent_fork
initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. If you are still online when it finishes, the runtime automatically delivers its completion notice. The notice includes the final answer unless the child sent you a message just before finishing. Use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display. Use the language of the user's current request.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

initial.name: wait_agent
initial.description: Wait for input at your next step, including agent messages, completion notifications, and user steering. Returns immediately when that input is already pending.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

initial.name: web_fetch
initial.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

initial.name: web_search
initial.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–10 search queries; their results are merged.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

initial.name: write
initial.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
